items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest combination approach, where variables from different sources are concatenated one after the other into a single new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the planned baseline-plus-concatenation design: build one model per method first, then concatenate the rescaled IR and fluorescence spectra into one matrix. The fused model should then be compared against those single-method baselines on held-out samples.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The review is a general PAT treatment, not the chicken-tissue study itself, and does not state that fusion improves performance for any particular system.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: Before fusing data from multiple sources, the contribution of each dataset and its complementarity should be evaluated.
items.how_it_applies: This justifies the planned step of establishing per-method baseline models before concatenation, so the added value of the fluorescence channel can be judged against the best single method.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general methodological recommendation from a PAT review, not evidence that IR and fluorescence are complementary for biological tissue classification.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E02 ¶82

items.finding: A cited Raman and FT-IR food analytical study showed that instrument complementarity was in some situations not sufficient to improve predictive performance for several quality attributes.
items.how_it_applies: This is a reason to test rather than assume: the fused model must demonstrably beat the best single-method model on held-out samples, otherwise the extra fluorescence channel should be dropped, as the plan already specifies.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited example concerns Raman and FT-IR on food samples, not MIR ATR and fluorescence on chicken muscle, fat and liver, so the outcome may differ for this system.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E02 ¶36
